caption: One gigabyte moves through the program 64 KB at a time: the read stream fills a single buffer, pipe() hands that chunk on, and the reader waits whenever the writer is full. Peak memory stays near 64 KB instead of 1024 MB.

spec.aria: A 1 GB file is read in 64 KB chunks by a read stream and passed through a buffer to a write stream, so only one chunk sits in memory at a time before the copy is written to disk.
